> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Round 4 adds the missing groom call-site regression without weakening the implementation approved in round 3. The new fixture supplies an earlier proven-bot application and a later actor that is neither proven automation nor a proven maintainer, then checks both the no-write outcome and the explicit `not provably machine-applied` refusal. This makes the newest-applier/consumer wiring load-bearing and distinguishes the target behavior from mere absence of any bot event. The shared ownership implementation remains fail-closed: only positive bot/App/caller-declared automation proof yields MACHINE; malformed App metadata is UNKNOWN through the I/O wrapper and raises through the pure path; human, unknown, and unattributable applications cannot authorize deletion. I found no new correctness, soundness, test-validity, or security issue in the diff.
